approach.method_basis: The Parent samples novel molecules directly from a task-local neural flow policy, then performs two graph refinement phases using accepted policy molecules and their descendants. A fingerprint Gaussian posterior chooses fresh graph offspring for evaluation while protecting the initial fresh-policy handoff. Every accepted encodable molecule retains its real score and exact token trajectory in a rank-sampled archive. Trajectory-balance updates jointly train the policy and a normalizer, with a categorical reference penalty toward a frozen prior. That prior is selected along unchanged unlabeled training by fixed-noise valid, connected, unique generation yield, using original holdout loss as the tie breaker. The present reference penalty averages token differences using the adapting policy probabilities.
approach.novelty: Reverse the direction of that one reference penalty so the frozen prior probabilities weight the token differences. This keeps a restoring gradient on a prior-supported alternative even when the adapting policy nearly abandons it, while keeping accepted-score trajectory balance and rank replay intact. The lineage has tested prior preparation, posterior selection and a scaffold replay mixture; this child instead changes how the fixed prior resists loss of its conditional token support. The test measures the changed gradient, actual reference divergence and later valid novel generation separately, because stronger retention may also weaken useful score adaptation.

observed_bottleneck: The current Parent n-dd7b8aa31113 uses the categorical KL(policy || frozen prior) at accepted replay prefixes. Its probability weighting makes the reference force vanish on a token as the policy assigns that token nearly zero probability, even if the frozen prior still supports it. This is a property of the implemented gradient, not evidence that a particular omitted token caused a particular invalid molecule. The complete Parent panel has mean 0.5501977216134929 and SD 0.02173839408580094. Across 230400 sampled replay members, recorded policy-to-prior KL averages 0.427377 before and 0.429185 after updates, reaching 1.895758; mean squared trajectory-balance residual before updates is 29.554839. Initial-feedback mean post-update KL is about 0.029 to 0.052 across sessions, with larger later values in every session. Only 8156 of 12000 raw neural draws are valid terminated molecules. The recent sibling n-0f40023ef64e confirms that broader scaffold replay reaches learning but also reduces graph-origin learning mass and high-score rank emphasis; both successful formal seeds lose score and the third lacks a valid macro score after an inherited terminal identity-join failure. The proposed bottleneck is therefore the reference penalty losing restorative influence over downweighted prior-supported token alternatives, while preserving the Parent score-focused replay distribution. Neither the loss magnitudes nor the validity rates establish KL direction as the existing cause of failure.
hypothesis: Replace the accepted-prefix categorical reference penalty KL(policy || frozen prior) with KL(frozen prior || policy), preserving the existing coefficient, sequence normalization, score-ranked replay and trajectory-balance objective.

finding_summary.headline: Restoring gradients activated, but retained support worsened and mean score fell
finding_summary.insights:
A restoring component on nearly abandoned prior-supported alternatives was present, yet that component alone did not preserve conditional support under these joint score-driven updates. This rules out an unchanged KL orientation, a drifting prior, missing graph feedback or altered replay labels as explanations for the outcome. The registered retention-benefit falsifier is triggered even though mechanism execution is confirmed. The loss can improve while its reference-divergence component worsens; changing direction at the inherited coefficient therefore does not establish the intended protection.

The small gain in valid novel strings cannot be credited to demonstrated support retention. Its seed dependence, the missing parent prior-to-policy diagnostic and the different search histories leave that causal connection unresolved. Graph-bearing policy movement and later scaffold matches increased, which also argues against explaining the score loss as a simple shutdown of graph-to-policy learning. The molecular assessment still found a mixture of plausible compact molecules and oversized or chemically questionable assemblies. The experiment therefore narrows the next question to how joint training can retain useful conditional support without losing objective progress; changing the reference gradient alone did not settle it.
finding_summary.results:
The reference gradient changed in all 7,185 updates after the policy and prior differed; the 15 identical initial states correctly showed no gradient difference. That activation did not produce better measured retention. Across 230,400 replay occurrences, prior-to-policy KL rose from 0.473648 before updates to 0.475468 afterward, and total variation rose from 0.215919 to 0.216668. Both average changes were unfavorable in every task-seed session. The inherited policy-to-prior diagnostic was also higher than the parent overall, although the two runs followed different histories.

Raw valid novel emission increased slightly, from 7,991 to 8,050 of 12,000 draws, or 66.59% to 67.08%. Mean accepted policy-origin score increased from 0.204941 to 0.222083, and graph feedback continued to affect later generation. Nevertheless, the three-seed mean final score fell from 0.550198 to 0.543814, a decrease of 0.006384. Paired seed changes were +0.000428, -0.027151 and +0.007572. The main final-score losses were in zaleplon_mpo and median_2, whose task means fell by 0.024000 and 0.020793. All fifteen task replicas completed their 300 evaluations.

molecular.headline: Compact phenolic amines coexist with oversized heteroaryl assemblies, tautomeric unsaturated rings and reactive bond motifs
molecular.overall_character: The supplied trajectories contain all five tasks and all three seeds, with 900 evaluated molecules and 870 optimizer proposals per task. All 4,350 optimizer-proposal SMILES parse with RDKit. Ring construction is abundant: digest ring-closure rates are 0.9828-0.9943 and aromatic-token rates 0.8368-0.9851. In task order, proposal median heavy-atom counts are 25, 35, 33, 32 and 24, and median ring counts are three, four, four, five and three. The output ranges from recognizable phenolic polycycles with tertiary aminoalkyl groups to partially unsaturated N/O heterocycles, large aminoheteroaryl ether/thioether assemblies, sulfonylated fused ring systems and fluorinated imino heterocycles. Unusual local bonds are not confined to negligible fragments: one task has 109 O-halogen proposals and 68 with O-O single bonds, while another has 77 C=C=N cumulene proposals, 72 contained in a perceived ring of at most seven atoms. Such graphs do not establish stable realizable compounds. Per-task nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts of 497-693 indicate substantial graph diversity, but the highest displayed molecules often occupy close analogue families. Parent chemistry already included elaborate heteroaryl assemblies, phenolic polycyclic amines and fused carbonyl systems; the current leaders change their local topology and substitution without resolving all chemical plausibility issues. No proposal has assigned stereocentres, despite 395, 227, 559, 350 and 315 proposals with unassigned centres in task order. The overall chemical reading is therefore mixed: plausible conventional subsets, substantial unresolved synthesis and geometry questions, and no experimental stability or activity evidence.

per_task.generated_character: The displayed leaders form a compact three-ring family: a central phenyl ether joins a partially unsaturated nitrogen ring bearing an aminoalkene to a cyano-substituted unsaturated oxygen ring. The top molecule has 24 heavy atoms and three six-membered rings, but only the phenyl ring is aromatic by RDKit perception. Nearby variants change ring size, replace oxygen with sulfur or carbon, alter imine/enamine positions, or add chlorine, fluorine or hydroxyl groups. This differs from the parent leaders, which included more aromatic indole-amide and fused heterocyclic systems. Full proposals remain aromatic-rich overall, with median two aromatic rings, so the single aromatic ring in this leading family should not be generalized to the whole output. Nitriles and aryl ethers are familiar chemistry; the aminoalkene/imine and unsaturated heterocycle combinations need qualification for tautomerism, geometry and synthetic access.
liabilities: Aminoalkene/imine and cyclic enol-ether-like units create tautomeric and potential reactivity questions; objective values do not establish stable solution species.
Thirty-seven proposals contain an O-O single bond and 17 contain an N-halogen bond, although those motifs are not required by the highest displayed structure.
Repeated scaffold elaboration can destroy the useful size and polar-group arrangement while preserving recognizable fragments of the original molecule.
missing_features: The leading neighborhood lacks broad, chemically established alternatives that retain its useful ether, nitrile and nitrogen placement while resolving the tautomeric unsaturated-ring architecture.
The highest structure has an unspecified stereocentre, and substituted or ring-contracted variants often add further unassigned centres; their three-dimensional configurations are not defined.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The top arrangement scores 0.478913. Replacing the oxygen within its cyano-bearing ring with carbon in a displayed terminal counterpart gives 0.337484, supporting the importance of that heteroatom environment within this local framework. Replacing the aryl ether link with a peroxide gives 0.443831, so the O-O bond is tolerated but is not supported as beneficial in that pair. Adding another nitrogen between the aminoalkene and ring gives 0.406646. Duplicating much of the motif in terminal products drops scores to approximately 0.000360 and 0.000660. Small species such as the isolated chlorine SMILES and fluorocyclobutane score zero, while large elaborate molecules also reach zero or vanishing values. These observations favor a specific intermediate-size heteroatom arrangement rather than maximal aromaticity, ring count or molecular growth.

per_task.generated_character: The highest family consists of extensive aminoheteroaryl ether assemblies bearing multiple aryl chlorine/bromine substituents, aminoalkyl or aminoalkenyl ether arms and quinazoline-like nitrogen heterocycles. The top molecule contains 55 heavy atoms, six aromatic rings and molecular mass 888.434. A different high-scoring family is a smaller heteroaryl thioether bearing a carbonyl nitrogen heterocycle, chloroethyl ether and imine/hydrazone-like substituents; one such molecule has 36 heavy atoms and mass 546.396. Displayed expansions reach ten or eleven aromatic rings. These are graph-valid combinations of recognizable fragments, but several whole structures are unusually large and carry chemically labile motifs. The parent also contained high-scoring extended aminoheteroaryl systems and frequent unusual oxygen connections. Current O-O single-bond proposals number 68 versus 135 in the parent, while O-halogen proposals number 109 versus 93; both remain material chemical liabilities.
liabilities: There are 172 proposals above 50 heavy atoms, with a maximum of 108; dense aromatic surfaces and heavy halogens make many high-scoring structures far larger than typical small-molecule chemotypes.
The population contains 109 O-halogen proposals, 68 with O-O single bonds, 11 acid halides and 13 carbon sites matching C(=N)-halogen, all chemically distinct from ordinary aryl halogenation.
The digest charged rate is 0.2287, with terminal nitro, anionic heteroaryl, azide and peroxide examples; formal graph validity does not settle their stability, synthesis or physical properties.
missing_features: The productive heteroaryl relationship lacks consistently economical, chemically stable whole-molecule realizations; near-equal scores occur across markedly different sizes and questionable terminal functionalities.
Imine and enamine geometries are unspecified, and stable replacements for peroxide, O-halogen and reactive imidoyl-halide connections are not demonstrated across the leading neighborhood.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The 55-heavy-atom assembly scores 0.844593 and the 36-heavy-atom thioether example 0.844527, showing that the largest construction is not uniquely necessary for the displayed score. Expanding an assembly to 84 heavy atoms and ten aromatic rings gives 0.844152, and an eleven-aromatic-ring structure scores 0.839275. Additional size therefore brings no clear reward in these examples. A peroxide-containing analogue still reaches 0.842353, and an imidoyl-chloride-like substituent also appears near the maximum; the score does not establish chemical stability. Lower-scoring cyclic or acyclic sulfone-rich structures lie near 0.258-0.301, despite substantial heteroatom or aromatic content. Terminal nitrogen-rich heteroaryl structures around 0.57-0.59 show that generic heteroaryl proliferation is insufficient to reproduce the higher-score arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule is a phenolic dibenzocycloheptane-like framework carrying a dimethylaminoethyl substituent: 21 heavy atoms, three rings, two aromatic rings and molecular mass 281.399. Its tertiary amine is on an acyclic side chain rather than inside a saturated ring. A propyl-linked analogue and more bridged phenolic ring variants also lead. These relatively compact structures are recognizable medicinal chemistry. Other seeds supply aryl-substituted cyclic amines and substantially larger piperazine/enamine/thioketone combinations, the latter prominent in the terminal digest. The parent also had strong phenolic polycyclic amines and arylpiperazine-linked aromatics. The current compact leaders simplify some of that chemistry, even though the full proposal distribution has median 33 heavy atoms and four rings versus parent medians of 30 and four.
liabilities: More bridged ring topologies introduce stereochemical and conformational questions absent from the simpler leading structure.
Terminal piperazine structures can include thioketones, thiols, enamines and additional N-S connections; their scores do not establish the practical stability of that combined functionality.
Thirty-five proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, despite a leading conventional phenolic amine of only 21 heavy atoms.
missing_features: No additional mandatory functional group can be inferred from the near-ceiling phenolic-amine scores; broader economical coverage of the demonstrated aromatic/amine arrangements is the supported chemical need.
The highest tricycle is achiral, but bridged analogues and complex cyclic-amine products have unspecified centres: 559 proposals contain an unassigned stereocentre and none assigns one.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The dimethylaminoethyl phenolic tricycle scores 0.999994 and the propyl-linked counterpart 0.999984. A ring-contracted aromatic analogue remains at 0.995878; adding extra halogen, amino or imino substitution does not establish a necessary improvement. The shared chemical association is a basic tertiary amine positioned with an aromatic phenolic framework. Low examples include amide/sulfonamide-rich aromatics and an acylhydrazone around 3.80e-05 to 9.56e-05, showing that nitrogen abundance alone is insufficient. A terminal piperazine/enamine/thioketone structure reaches 0.993165, but a much larger duplicated nitrogen-linked assembly drops to 0.029234. These observations support contextual amine placement and controlled elaboration, not experimentally established binding or a requirement for ring-bound nitrogen.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family combines a sulfonylated saturated nitrogen ring fused to a pyrrole- or pyrazole-like ring, a methylenedioxyphenyl substituent and a fused diazaaromatic arm. The top example has 36 heavy atoms, six rings, four aromatic rings and molecular mass 504.612; close relatives change sulfonyl alkyl length, ring nitrogen placement or the aromatic connecting arm. Sulfonylation means the saturated ring nitrogen should not be read as an ordinary basic piperidine nitrogen. Another leading family comprises densely fused N-methyl cyclic carbonyl systems, sometimes bearing an azetidine ether. The parent also produced fused cyclic carbonyl and sulfonamide-containing aromatic chemotypes. Current full proposals have median 32 heavy atoms and five rings, with 693 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds; these are abundant but often structurally elaborate ring systems.
liabilities: Many six-ring leaders approach or exceed molecular mass 500, and 55 proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, creating substantial size and synthetic-complexity burdens.
Dense fused carbonyl and aromatic systems can impose conformational or synthetic constraints that ring counts and accepted SMILES do not characterize.
Sulfonylated nitrogens, aromatic nitrogens and pyrrolic NH groups have different electronic roles; simply adding nitrogen cannot be interpreted as increasing useful basic centres.
missing_features: The leading chemical region lacks broad simpler alternatives that retain its combination of aromatic, sulfonyl and nitrogen-containing ring relationships.
Regioisomeric and stereochemical coverage is incomplete: the highest sulfonylated fused-ring molecule has an unspecified stereocentre, and 350 proposals have at least one unassigned centre.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The propylsulfonyl fused-ring example scores 0.230034 and its ethylsulfonyl counterpart 0.227223. Pyrazole-related sulfonamide variants lie near 0.220-0.226. Those nearby scores support a shared multi-ring/polar arrangement more strongly than a specific extra alkyl carbon. Adding another sulfonyl connection produces a larger 40-heavy-atom example at 0.224826, so extra sulfur/oxygen and size are not sufficient. Low molecules include methane at zero, small sulfur or oxygen compounds near 0.009 and a long-chain hydroxylated ring at 0.034939. Terminal fused carbonyl structures reach about 0.172-0.204 but do not establish that adding fusion alone supplies the missing arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule is a compact tertiary amine joining a gem-difluorinated annulated triazole/ether system to a bridged azaaromatic ring system. It has 25 heavy atoms, five rings and one unspecified stereocentre. Other leaders contain pyridyl-substituted imino nitrogen heterocycles with methoxyamino or methoxymethylamino groups. A chemically distinct leader has an acylguanidine-like side chain and thiol attached through oxygen to a fluorinated seven-membered ring containing a C=C=N cumulene. That molecule has 23 heavy atoms and no aromatic rings by RDKit, despite aromatic-rich alternatives elsewhere in the same task. The parent leaders likewise mixed fused nitrogen heterocycles and unusual fluorinated unsaturated sulfur/nitrogen chemistry. Current proposals have median 24 heavy atoms and three rings; this is primarily a local bonding and configuration problem rather than pervasive molecular overgrowth.
liabilities: Seventy-seven proposals contain C=C=N, and 72 place that motif within a perceived ring of at most seven atoms. This is a ketenimine-like heterocumulene, not an all-carbon allene; its reactivity and ring geometry require chemical qualification.
Methoxyamino N-O bonds, thioaldehyde-like or thiol substituents, and unusual fused ring connectivity introduce different stability or synthetic-access questions in different leading families.
The highest bridged amine has unspecified configuration, and the trajectories provide no measurements of stability, physical properties or synthetic accessibility.
missing_features: The higher-score regions lack demonstrated stable ring and substituent alternatives preserving their useful compact polar arrangement, especially around the cyclic cumulene and densely bridged nitrogen systems.
Imine/enamine and heterocumulene geometry is not specified, while 315 proposals contain an unassigned stereocentre; graph connectivity alone leaves important molecular configurations unresolved.
No unique mandatory basic group, aromatic ring count or fluorinated target-like motif is justified because several chemically distinct leading families are visible.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The bridged tertiary-amine structure scores 0.434778 and a pyridyl imino heterocycle with a methoxyamino group 0.412986. Replacing that N-O-containing substituent with the displayed N-methoxymethyl variant gives 0.407779, showing that a direct N-O bond is not uniquely required for a nearby score. The cyclic C=C=N structure scores 0.401017; related terminal structures range from 0.021065 to 0.319810 as ring nitrogen, linkage and side-chain placement change. The score therefore recognizes some compact polar arrangements while tolerating unusual local chemistry; it does not establish the realizability of a cyclic cumulene. Oversized glycosylated, peptide-like or highly elaborated aromatic examples are zero or extremely small. The full trajectory median is 0.0024005953 and exactly two rows are zero, so the distribution is weak overall without being a population of literal zeros.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One proposal set contains 109 O-halogen motifs, 68 O-O single bonds, 11 acid halides and 13 C(=N)-halogen motifs, with a peroxide and imidoyl-halide-like functionality present near its highest scores. Another set contains 77 C=C=N cumulenes, 72 within perceived rings of at most seven atoms, including a displayed molecule scoring 0.401017. Elsewhere, the aryl ether leader scores 0.478913 while its peroxide analogue scores 0.443831, so a labile bond is not necessarily rewarded even when tolerated.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain chemically stable local bonds and geometrically credible unsaturation in useful neighborhoods.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing capability is dependable access to ordinary, stable alternatives preserving an observed useful arrangement of rings and polar groups. Distinguish aryl halogens from oxygen or reactive imidoyl halides, ethers from peroxides, and conventional imines from constrained heterocumulenes, without relying on any objective identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The five proposal sets contain one, 172, 35, 55 and five molecules above 50 heavy atoms. In one leading family, 55- and 36-heavy-atom structures both score approximately 0.8445, while expansion to 84 heavy atoms and ten aromatic rings yields 0.844152. A conventional phenolic amine reaches near-ceiling score with 21 heavy atoms, whereas a duplicated nitrogen-linked assembly in that session scores 0.029234. Duplicating another compact heterocyclic motif produces scores near 0.000360 and 0.000660.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent economical control of size and repetition around productive chemical cores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve chemical alternatives with controlled ring fusion, linker length, appendage count and molecular mass. The output needs contextual growth around a useful arrangement, since compact and extended structures can both be productive but repeated elaboration often contributes size without an evident chemical benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: No assigned stereocentres occur among 4,350 optimizer proposals. The five sessions contain 395, 227, 559, 350 and 315 proposals with at least one unassigned centre. Leaders include partially unsaturated heterocycles, bridged phenolic systems, sulfonylated fused rings and a bridged tertiary amine. Numerous imine, enamine and heterocumulene motifs introduce further geometry questions. The simplest leading phenolic tricycle is achiral, so the issue is conditional rather than universal.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator proposes stereogenic and configurationally flexible chemistry without defining the relevant configurations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support chemically consistent explicit stereoisomers and bond geometries when those degrees of freedom exist, while preserving access to achiral structures. The available feedback does not specify which unobserved configuration should be preferred, and graph validity alone does not define a three-dimensional proposal.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Per-session nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts range from 497 to 693. Nevertheless, digest leaders repeatedly vary an aminoalkene/cyano-heterocycle arrangement, large aminoheteroaryl assemblies, phenolic tertiary amines, six-ring sulfonylated systems or compact fluorinated nitrogen heterocycles. Close local changes can matter: replacing a cyano-bearing ring oxygen with carbon accompanies a decrease from 0.478913 to 0.337484. Amide or sulfonamide nitrogen environments also differ sharply from the useful tertiary-amine environment visible in another session.
transferable_gaps.gap: Many graph scaffolds coexist with narrow productive families and incomplete transfer of useful functional-group arrangements to alternative cores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically distinct core and linker alternatives that preserve relevant polar-group position and electronic context, beyond repeated peripheral substitution or ring closure. Nitrogen count, aromaticity and scaffold identity are insufficient descriptions of useful chemistry; the generator needs coverage of how those features are connected.

method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.
